reviews.text: The apartment's rules are interesting — acoustic dead zones that migrate seasonally, desire paths nobody walked, a window that switches views — but the story never commits to systematizing them, and that's a problem for me. Linnea has eleven years of data and twenty-three notebooks but we never learn what the rules actually are. The 'don't formalize it or it changes' bit feels like a dodge to avoid building a coherent system. Character work is fine. Prose is fine. But a story about someone obsessively mapping phenomena should give us more of the map.
